recorder.sentence: Every book supplies its time with one good word; every municipal law, every trade, every folly of the day, and the generic catholic genius who is not afraid or ashamed to owe his originality to the originality of all, stands with the next age as the recorder and embodiment of his own.

recorder.author: Bram Stoker

recording.author: Charles Darwin
recording.sentence: Hence I look at individual differences, though of small interest to the systematist, as of high importance for us, as being the first step towards such slight varieties as are barely thought worth recording in works on natural history.

recording.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
recording.sentence: The poet, in utter solitude remembering his spontaneous thoughts and recording them, is found to have recorded that which men in cities vast find true for them also.

subcutaneous.author: Bram Stoker

uncordial.author: Jane Austen

uncut.author: James Joyce

unrecorded.author: Herman Melville
unrecorded.sentence: For in their succourless empty-handedness, they, in the heathenish sharked waters, and by the beaches of unrecorded, javelin islands, battled with virgin wonders and terrors that Cook with all his marines and muskets would not willingly have dared.
